title: HubSpot Review (2026)
intro: HubSpot is an AI-powered customer platform best known for free forever CRM plus paid Sales, Marketing, and Service hubs. This review covers verified Free CRM and Smart CRM/Customer Platform pricing, the separate Sales Hub ladder, core capabilities, limitations, and who should buy — based on official first-party sources.
summary: HubSpot is a strong freemium CRM platform choice when you want free core CRM with suite upside. Scores reflect live first-party research — not hands-on product testing.
verdict: HubSpot is a strong freemium CRM platform for teams that want free forever core CRM with a clear upgrade path into Sales, Marketing, and Service hubs. Value is excellent at Free/Starter, but packaging complexity and per-seat hub costs grow quickly on Professional/Enterprise. This review is based on first-party product pages and HubSpot’s Product & Services Catalog — not hands-on product testing.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Free CRM and Starter entry are marketed as approachable, but HubSpot’s multi-hub seat model and Professional/Enterprise admin surfaces raise the learning curve as teams expand beyond core CRM.
Deal pipelines are included on Free CRM, and Sales Hub pages emphasize pipeline/deal management, prospecting workspace, and deal scores as core sales workflows.
Sales Hub documents playbooks, personalized email sequences, and AI-assisted prospecting; automation depth increases on paid hubs versus Free CRM alone.

Catalog and Sales Hub pages document email scheduling, tracking, and sequences; HubSpot is strong for sales email workflows within the CRM, with Marketing Hub as a separate (paid) email marketing pillar.
Reporting dashboard is listed on Free CRM; Sales Analytics & Reporting and AI forecasting are documented on Sales Hub paid tiers.
Starter adds required fields/permission sets; Professional adds scoring/calculated properties/custom reporting; Enterprise adds custom objects, SSO, and field-level permissions.

First-party Marketplace is a core platform story for connecting apps across the customer platform; exact app counts were not re-verified on researched pages, but integration breadth is a documented strength.
Seat types (Core vs Sales), multiple hubs, onboarding fees on higher hub tiers, and promo vs list pricing create real packaging/admin overhead versus simpler single-product CRMs.
Enterprise hub features (SSO, custom objects, field-level permissions, quotas/approvals) and multi-hub platform design support mid-market and enterprise GTM orgs.
Genuine free forever CRM plus approachable Starter Customer Platform pricing is strong value; costs rise quickly when Sales Hub Professional/Enterprise and additional hubs are required for full GTM.

faq.question: How much does HubSpot cost?
faq.answer: HubSpot Free CRM is $0 with no credit card required. The Customer Platform/Smart CRM marketing ladder starts at $15/seat/mo* for Starter (catalog list $20), then $50 Professional and $75 Enterprise. Sales Hub is priced separately: Starter $20 list, Professional $100/month per seat on the catalog and Sales product page (HubSpot’s Sales pricing page also shows $90/mo/seat billed annually vs $100 monthly), and Enterprise $150/seat/mo billed annually. Always confirm live HubSpot checkout.

faq.question: Is HubSpot CRM really free?
faq.answer: Yes. HubSpot documents Free CRM as 100% free with no expiration date and no credit card required, including contact management, deal pipelines, CRM import, Breeze Assistant, and a reporting dashboard. Paid seats unlock more permissions, scoring, custom objects, and hub features.

faq.question: Are the $15/$50/$75 prices Sales Hub seats?
faq.answer: Not exactly. Those figures appear on HubSpot’s Free CRM / Customer Platform marketing page and align with Smart CRM Professional/Enterprise catalog list prices ($50/$75), with Starter shown as a $15* new-customer promo versus $20 catalog list. Sales Hub has its own ladder ($20 / $100 Professional / $150).

faq.question: Does HubSpot offer a free trial?
faq.answer: Sales Hub pages include a CTA to start a 14-day free trial of HubSpot’s sales tools, in addition to the permanent Free CRM tier.

faq.question: Is this a hands-on SoftwareGlimpse lab review?
faq.answer: No. This review is approved from first-party HubSpot product pages and the Product & Services Catalog. SoftwareGlimpse has not recorded hands-on product testing for HubSpot in this assessment.

sections.heading: What HubSpot is
sections.body: HubSpot positions itself as an agentic customer platform: free Smart CRM at the center, with optional Marketing, Sales, Service, Content, Data, and Revenue hubs. Buyers often start on Free CRM and expand into paid seats/hubs without migrating data.

sections.heading: Pricing and plans
sections.body: Document two ladders. (1) Free CRM + Smart CRM/Customer Platform seats from the CRM marketing page: Free $0, Starter from $15/seat/mo*, Professional $50, Enterprise $75 — asterisk denotes new-customer discount; catalog Smart CRM Starter list is $20. (2) Sales Hub: Free $0, Starter $20 list, Professional $100/month per seat on catalog and the Sales product page, Enterprise $150 billed annually. HubSpot’s Sales pricing page also shows Professional $90/mo/seat billed annually vs $100 monthly. Prices are USD per seat per month as published.

sections.heading: Core CRM capabilities
sections.body: Free CRM covers contacts, deal pipelines, import, Breeze Assistant, and reporting. Paid Customer Platform seats add permissions, scoring, custom reporting, and Enterprise governance (custom objects, SSO, field-level permissions). Sales Hub adds prospecting, sequences, playbooks, forecasting, and deal analytics.

sections.heading: Who it’s for
sections.body: Best for teams that want freemium CRM with suite upside. Less ideal if you need simple single-product sales CRM pricing or dialer-first engagement as the core story.

productExperience.summary: Based on HubSpot’s documented product story, teams typically start on Free CRM for contacts and deal pipelines, use Breeze Assistant for AI help, then add Sales Hub seats for prospecting, sequences, forecasting, and denser analytics as the motion matures.
